title: plugin
description: Native code, described: the settings a project may pass it, and what it grants -- ports (native), trigger kinds, connection kinds, codecs, shapes. Everything effectful enters through a grant. A plugin is an alias root: @http/http.port.json.

$schema.description: The kind of this document: its published schema URL, or the alias @wilanis/plugin.schema.json.

description.description: What this plugin is for, in one or two sentences, shown wherever a reader meets it.

label.description: A short human name for this document, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its path. Absent: the file name stands in.

grants.description: What the plugin grants a tree: everything effectful enters through one of these, and each is a file under the plugin's docs/ that a reader can open.

ports.description: The native ports it grants, by path. A tree names their operations from a graph and never binds them; the plugin implements them.

triggerKinds.description: The trigger kinds it grants, by path. A trigger of one of these kinds fires a domain operation when something outside happens.

connectionKinds.description: The connection kinds it grants, by path. A connection of one of these kinds says how to reach one outside system.

codecs.description: The codecs it grants, by path. A codec reads a body into values and writes values back out.

shapes.description: The shapes it grants, by path, for contracts and documents to name.

requires.description: What the plugin calls but does not implement: each is a file under the plugin's docs/, and the host binds it in a feature of its own, as it binds any domain port (B002 until it does).

ports.description: The ports it requires, by path. The plugin calls their operations; a profile binds each to a binding the host writes. A path is granted or required, never both (D012).

guard.description: Declared by the one plugin that identifies callers. `credentials` are what it verifies -- token, challenge -- each with the type a trigger's policy attachment must give it and the context fields it yields once verified; `context` is what it adds to every trigger kind's context: request.principal, request.session, request.challenge, what policies and resolvers read. `refuses` lists the reasons it refuses with on its own (a credential that does not verify), each with what it means; a trigger giving a credential must map them (T005).

refuses.description: The reasons the guard refuses with on its own, by name, each with what it means. A trigger that gives it a credential must map them (T005).

credentials.description: What the guard verifies, by name -- a token, a challenge -- each with the type a trigger's policy attachment must give it.

yields.description: The context fields this credential yields once it verifies, which policies and resolvers may then read.

description.description: What this credential is, for a reader deciding which one a trigger should hand over.
